gotchas.procedure_section: Schedule E / Rental Properties; Scan - Schedule E records (hours log)
gotchas.title: Short-term rental: not a 'rental activity'; material participation
gotchas.trap: Treat the Airbnb condo as a passive rental: loss suspended on Form 8582 (MAGI < $100k -> maybe $25k allowance) or move it to Schedule C with SE tax.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Average stay 3.10 nights (<= 7) -> not a rental activity (Reg. 1.469-1T(e)(3)(ii)(A)); no substantial services -> stays on Schedule E (no SE tax). Handwritten log: 180 hours, more than any other individual (cleaner ~95) -> material participation test 3 -> nonpassive. Loss ($15,147) offsets wages; no Form 8582.
gotchas.impact: Sch 1 line 5 ($15,147); tax effect ~22% of the loss

gotchas.title: Airbnb 1099-K gross vs payouts vs occupancy taxes
gotchas.trap: Report the organizer's payout figure $48,447 (and still deduct host fees = double deduction), or treat the occupancy/sales tax column as income and a deduction.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Rents = 1099-K gross $49,945 (nightly + cleaning fees), host fees $1,498 deducted once; occupancy/sales taxes $6,368 collected and remitted by Airbnb are neither income nor deductible. Reconciled CSV to 1099-K.

gotchas.procedure_section: Schedule E / Rental Properties - personal use days
gotchas.title: Personal-use days: 280A allocation, not the vacation-home limit
gotchas.trap: Ignore the girls' trip (deduct 100% of all expenses) or treat the condo as a vacation home and limit expenses to income.
gotchas.correct_treatment: 6 personal days < greater of 14 / 10% of 192 -> not a residence; shared expenses x 192/198. Personal share of property tax ($66) to Sch A; personal share of mortgage interest ($429) is nondeductible personal interest (condo not a qualified residence). Maintenance days are not personal days.
gotchas.impact: Sch E expenses; Sch A line 5b

gotchas.procedure_section: Schedule E / Rental Properties - capitalization of repairs; Scan - spreadsheet
gotchas.title: Client spreadsheet expenses closing costs, furniture and personal items
gotchas.trap: Deduct the spreadsheet as-is: closing costs, $24.6k furniture as 'supplies', full property-tax bill, occupancy taxes, Dollywood pass, gas receipts.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Capitalize acquisition costs into basis ($388,410; land $58,262 per assessor ratio); building 39-yr MM (unit used on a transient basis is not a 'dwelling unit' for 27.5-yr); furniture 5-yr with 100% bonus (acquired after 01/19/2025) on Form 4562; loan costs amortized; property tax limited to her post-closing share $2,163 (IRC 164(d)); mileage at 70c replaces gas; Dollywood pass is personal.

gotchas.title: Gambling: gross winnings, losses capped, 2025 = 100%
gotchas.trap: Net the jackpot against losses and report nothing (client's view), or deduct $15,400, or apply the OBBBA 90% limit (procedure text says 'in effect for 2026').
gotchas.correct_treatment: Report $12,000 W-2G winnings on Sch 1 line 8b; losses deductible only as an itemized deduction (Sch A line 16) limited to winnings = $12,000. The 90% limit applies to tax years beginning after 12/31/2025 - not 2025. Procedure wording is imprecise; law followed.

gotchas.procedure_section: Schedule A - itemize vs standard / sales tax
gotchas.title: Itemizing only works because of the gambling losses
gotchas.trap: Take the standard deduction (as in 2024) - losing the gambling-loss deduction and taxing $12,000 of winnings in full.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Itemized $23,992 (sales tax - TN has no income tax - + real estate tax + home mortgage + charity + gambling) vs standard $15,750; without gambling itemized would be $11,992.

gotchas.procedure_section: Schedule A - Disaster Losses (federally declared only)
gotchas.title: Windstorm tree damage is not deductible
gotchas.trap: Deduct the $1,000 deductible and $2,400 tree removal as a casualty loss.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Personal casualty losses for 2025 are deductible only if attributable to a federally declared disaster (Form 4684); the 07/18/2025 storm had no declaration (insurer letter). Expansion to state-declared disasters starts 2026. $0; no gain because reimbursement did not exceed basis.

gotchas.title: NC nonresident return for NC-casino winnings
gotchas.trap: No state return because Tennessee has no income tax; the $510 NC withholding is lost (or claimed on the 1040).
gotchas.correct_treatment: Winnings from a North Carolina casino are NC-source; file D-400 as nonresident with Schedule PN: NC taxable income x 0.1347 -> tax $437 vs withholding $510 -> refund $73. NC does not allow gambling losses.
